subject.name_or_desc: A woman (the querent), of tall stature, ruddy complexioned, sober, discreet and well spoken

context.question: If she should marry the man desired?
context.asked_at: Anno 1646 (figure heading fragment); the day is not legible in the OCR.
context.setting: She desired to marry a particular man, who was very tall, slender and lean, of black hair, stood upon high terms, and had been tampering with another.

attachments.key_positions: Mercury, significatrix of the querent, retrograde and under the Sun-beams; the quesited's significator in his exaltation, neer the sextile of Venus; both significators in a semi-sextile and in good houses; the Moon separating from a square of Jupiter and carrying his light by a trine to Mercury, lord of the Ascendant
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. LX: if she should marry the man desired (printed pp.389–390; Fig. 15 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
